# Fontroom

> Fontroom is a free, open source font preview tool. Pick any Google Font or your own font file, see it on a realistic website, on your own live website and in a phone app, compare heading and body pairings, then copy the setup code for HTML and CSS, Tailwind, Next.js, Flutter or Expo. No account, nothing to install, MIT licensed.

Font sites show one sentence on a blank page. Real products have buttons, prices, menus and phone screens. Fontroom puts the font into those places so you can judge it before you change your code.

## Use it

- [Open Fontroom](https://fontroom.vercel.app/app): the font preview tool
- [Landing page](https://fontroom.vercel.app/): what it does, how it works and FAQ
- [Design primitives](https://fontroom.vercel.app/primitives): the tokens and components behind Fontroom
- [Source code](https://github.com/Tekcify/fontroom): MIT licensed, issues and contributions welcome

## What it does

- Preview any Google Font on sample sites (SaaS, café, docs, magazine) and a matching phone app, side by side.
- Preview fonts on your own live website: pick "Your website" under Site (shortcut L) and paste a link. It loads at desktop and phone widths with your fonts applied.
- Try your own .woff2, .woff, .ttf or .otf file. It is read in the browser and never uploaded.
- Set separate heading and body fonts, or press "Try a pairing" for a curated match.
- The weight menu lists only weights the font really has, so the browser never fakes a bold. Variable fonts are detected.
- Click any text in the preview to type your own words. Switch light and dark, size and accent colour.
- Save pairings in your browser and flip between them with [ and ].
- Share a link that holds both fonts, the weight, size, colour and theme, for example https://fontroom.vercel.app/app#h=Syne&b=Inter&w=700
- Get code for HTML and CSS, Tailwind, Next.js (next/font), Flutter (google_fonts) and Expo, loading only the weights you use.

## How to preview a font before using it

1. Open https://fontroom.vercel.app/app and search Google Fonts by name, or drop in your own file.
2. See it on the website and phone app. Click any text to type your own words.
3. Press "Get code" and copy the setup for your stack.

## FAQ

- Is Fontroom free? Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license. No account, nothing to install.
- Can I preview fonts on my own website? Yes. Pick "Your website" under Site, or press L, and paste a link. Some single page apps and sites behind bot checks may not load.
- Do my font files get uploaded? No. Your file is read in your browser and stays on your device. It is not added to share links or saved pairings.
- How do I find a good font pairing? Set a heading font and a body font, or press "Try a pairing". Save the ones you like and flip between them with [ and ].
- Does Fontroom support variable fonts? Yes. Google Font weight ranges are shown as they exist, and your own variable files are detected.
- Can I use these fonts in a commercial product? Google Fonts are open source, so almost always yes. Check the license on the font's Google Fonts page. For your own files, your font license applies.
- Which stacks does the code cover? Plain HTML and CSS, Tailwind, Next.js with next/font, Flutter with google_fonts, and Expo.
- Where are saved pairings kept? In your browser. Nothing goes to a server.

## Keyboard shortcuts

/ search, ↑ ↓ preview fonts, Enter keep, H or B edit headings or body, X swap, R random pairing, S save, [ ] flip saved pairings, D light or dark, 1 2 3 show both, website or app, U your own font file, L your website, C get code, ? show shortcuts.
